title: Find water at home
summary: Where there's hidden safe water in your house, and which sources to never drink.

cards.headline: The taps are dry. Where is safe water hiding?
cards.body: If your tap water was safe before it stopped, your water heater tank (not a heating boiler), the water in your pipes, melted ice cubes, and liquid from canned fruit and vegetables are usable.

cards.headline: Drain the water heater tank
cards.body: Turn off its power or gas first. Close the cold water intake valve, open a hot water faucet in the house, then open the drain at the bottom of the tank. Let the water cool first.

cards.headline: Refill the tank before turning it back on
cards.body: Refill the water heater before you turn its power or gas back on. If the gas was shut off, a professional needs to turn it back on.

cards.headline: Get the water left in your pipes
cards.body: Open the highest faucet in the house to let air in. Then collect water from the lowest faucet.

cards.headline: Don't drink pool or hot tub water
cards.body: Never drink from radiators, heating boilers, waterbeds, pools, or hot tubs. Pool and hot tub water is fine for washing and flushing. Toilet tank water (never the bowl) works if treated and free of cleaning tablets.

cards.headline: Know where your main water shutoff is
cards.body: If you hear of broken water or sewer lines, close the main valve to keep dirty water out of your pipes. Show everyone at home where it is.

cards.headline: Don't ration water unless officials tell you to
cards.body: Drink what you need today and look for more tomorrow. Most people need at least half a gallon a day to drink. Rest and stay cool to need less.

sources.title: FEMA, Are You Ready? (IS-22), sections 1.3 and 1.4: Water

cards.headline: Soda, coffee, and alcohol don't replace water
cards.body: Carbonated drinks don't count as drinking water. Caffeine and alcohol make you lose water, so you need even more.
